title: MCP boolean (and sequence) params are stringified by the chat harness dispatcher; only the `exec` sandbox preserves native JSON types
wanted_capability: Chat-harness MCP tool dispatch should preserve JSON argument types (booleans, numbers, nulls, arrays, objects) when serializing tool call arguments, OR every bbox tool with a boolean or array-typed param should accept both JSON `true`/`false` and the strings "true"/"false" (and JSON-encoded sequences) so call sites work regardless of dispatch path. Today the chat surface silently turns every boolean into the string "true"/"false" and every array into a JSON-encoded string before the daemon sees the argument, which fails the deserialize step with no signal at the call site beyond the raw "invalid type" error.
fallback_used: Wrapped the failing tool call in an `exec` cell so the JS value is serialized as a native JSON boolean/array, not the string "true" or a JSON-encoded array string. This is the same pattern used to file this very gap note (the first attempt failed with the identical string/sequence deserialize error).
evidence: session:7be994da-030f-4eb3-a0c7-65a8d9121e49 - direct chat-dispatcher call to mcp__blackbox__bbox_thread_list(include_resolved: true) returned: "failed to deserialize parameters: invalid type: string 'true', expected a boolean".
Same call issued from inside an `exec` JavaScript cell with the native JS boolean `true` succeeded.
First attempt to file bbox_gap with evidence: ["..."] was sent as evidence: "[\"...\"]" and produced "invalid type: string [...], expected a sequence".
